The core operators define a hierarchical probabilistic inference pipeline. First, a GAN model encodes positional and contextual features into a monotonic save probability, ensuring logical consistency with increasing defensive pressure. Second, historical save probabilities act as informative priors that bias the model toward realistic defensive behavior. Third, shot location modulates the base probability of scoring, conditioned on the defender's estimated save likelihood. These primitives form a dual structure: one rooted in generative modeling (GAN), the other in observational statistics (historical data). Failure modes arise when GANs overfit to training data or when historical data becomes non-representative. The interplay between these operators enables robust prediction under uncertainty, forming the basis for both conformal inference in GSI and dynamic state transitions in GSE.
